name: Heron Island
description: Heron Island, a coral cay near the Tropic of Capricorn in the southern Great Barrier Reef, 87 km north-east of Gladstone: about 800 m long and 300 m wide, with the University of Queensland's research station, a green turtle nesting ground and the wreck of HMCS Protector at the entrance to its boat channel. With Heron Reef and Wistari Reef, rebuilt from 30 m survey bathymetry and Sentinel-2; the cay's ground is rebuilt from its mapped outline.
area_note: 19.4 x 14.3 km: Heron Reef with the cay at its western end, Wistari Reef across the channel to the south-west, and the open water around them.

tide.note: MSQ lists Heron Island as a secondary place of Gladstone (80 km west-south-west, in the Port Curtis harbour) with high and low water 33 minutes earlier and 0.71 of its range. Bundaberg's standard port gauge at Burnett Heads (24 46 S 152 23 E, 153 km south-south-east) is used instead because its tide is closer to Heron's in both respects: MSQ's 2026 tidal planes put spring high and low water at +1.21 and -1.09 m about mean sea level at Heron Island, +1.16 and -1.17 m at Burnett Heads and +1.62 and -1.62 m at Gladstone, and in the 2026 fits Burnett Heads' M2 runs about 43 minutes ahead of Gladstone's, so about 10 minutes ahead of Heron's where Gladstone's lags by 33. Neither is an offshore gauge; times and heights at Heron Island differ from Burnett Heads' by those amounts. (The portal's 2024 and 2025 resources of the separate 'Burnett Heads' storm-surge gauge hold Bugatti Reef Outer's file, so they are not used.)

life.note: Coral cay profile for web/reef/life.js (format in web/reef/life/profile.js). Plants, from Wikipedia, Heron Island (Queensland): Pisonia grandis forest dominates the centre and south (most trees 6-8 m, some 10-11 m); north of it a band of open shrubland of octopus bush (Heliotropium foertherianum) and sea cabbage (Scaevola taccada) with Pandanus and Casuarina equisetifolia ssp. incana; the eastern end and the dune ridges Casuarina, Scaevola and Heliotropium with some Pandanus. Not drawn: Celtis, Ficus, Pipturus, Cordia, Suriana and the herbs. Turtles nesting: the same page (green 98%, loggerhead 2% of the nesters; the nesting area is the central part of the north shore, `around`); the months, November to March, are the ones Wikipedia gives for Lady Elliot Island in the same Capricorn-Bunker group (no Heron-specific source for the months was found); perKm is not sourced. Spawning: UQ News, 25 November 2003, 'Coral puts on show at Heron Island' (news.uq.edu.au/2003-11-25-coral-puts-show-heron-island): usually five to eight nights after the November full moon, one lunation after the inshore reefs' October (lag 1).
